title: Dinghy
body:
Dinghy is a small open boat, rowed, sailed, or powered by a small outboard motor, used as a tender for larger vessels and for short trips on sheltered water. Dinghies are light, easy to beach, and the first boat most sailors learn to handle.

The dinghy is the foundation of small-boat seamanship, and dinghy sailing remains the standard entry to the sport worldwide.

title: Sailboat
body:
Sailboat is a boat driven by sails, with a hull, a rig, and a keel or centreboard that lets it sail against the wind as well as before it. Sailboats range from single-handed dinghies to ocean-going yachts, and they are sailed for sport, transport, and long-distance cruising.

Sailing is one of humanity's oldest transport technologies, and the modern sailboat carries that history in a form refined by racing and cruising design.

title: Motorboat
body:
Motorboat is a boat driven by an inboard or outboard engine, built for speed, fishing, waterskiing, or patrol work. Motorboats trade the silence of sail for power and range, and they dominate inland lakes, rivers, and coastal work.

The motorboat reshaped recreational boating in the twentieth century, putting fast water transport within reach of ordinary owners.

title: Fishing Boat
body:
Fishing Boat is a working boat built to catch fish, with holds for the catch, gear for nets or lines, and a hull suited to its waters — from small inshore boats to ocean trawlers. Fishing boats are the oldest working craft still in daily use, and their forms vary by every coast on earth.

Fishing boats feed coastal communities, and their design is a direct record of local waters, species, and weather.

title: Ferry
body:
Ferry is a boat that carries passengers, vehicles, or both on a regular route across a river, harbour, or strait. Ferries are public transport on water, running to timetables, and they are essential where bridges or tunnels are impractical.

Ferries are among the most-used boats in the world, and large double-ended ferries carry thousands of passengers a day on short crossings.

title: Yacht
body:
Yacht is a pleasure boat, sailed or powered, built for comfort and speed on cruises and races. Yachts range from modest family cruisers to superyachts with crews, and the word covers both the vessel and the way of life around it.

Yachting grew from working sail into a sport and a leisure industry, with its own races, marinas, and design traditions.

title: Canoe and Kayak
body:
Canoe and Kayak are small paddle craft: a canoe is paddled from a kneeling or seated position with a single-bladed paddle, while a kayak is paddled seated with a double-bladed paddle. Both are ancient designs — the canoe from North American birch-bark craft, the kayak from Arctic skin boats — and both are now mass-produced in plastic and composite.

Canoes and kayaks are the most accessible boats of all, used for touring, whitewater sport, fishing, and wilderness travel.

title: Tugboat
body:
Tugboat is a small but powerful boat built to push or tow larger vessels, barges, and ships in harbours and along rivers. Tugboats have outsized engines for their size, strong towing gear, and hulls built for manoeuvring in tight water.

Without tugboats, large ships could not safely enter or leave port, and the tug is the unglamorous workhorse of every harbour.
